about: Curated, cached incentive/financing catalog for the HomeForge Funding Advisor. Screening rules are hints, not full statutory criteria; nothing here is an eligibility, tax, or award determination. verification: team_verified = team read the source on checked_on; spec_reference = from the team's agent spec, primary page not re-read; team_research_unverified = from the team's research table, no primary source linked yet.

programs.name: Nonprofit homeownership welfare exemption (RTC §214.15.1)
programs.how_it_works: May exempt property owned by a qualifying nonprofit that builds or rehabilitates homes for sale to low-income first-time buyers from property tax — a possible reduction of an expense, not a cash grant or a transferable credit.
programs.availability_note: BOE LTA 2023/044: operative for lien date January 1, 2023 through lien date January 1, 2027. As of the check date, only the 2027-01-01 lien date remains. (The team spec's 'before 2028' date is a separate construction deadline in the same letter.)

eligibility_rules.label: 45-year recorded agreement with the local agency meeting §214.15.1(a) terms
Units sold only to first-time homebuyers that are low-income families
Affordable housing cost ≤ 30% of gross income
eligibility_rules.conflict_note: The model assumes {value:pct} of income for housing; §214.15.1(d)(2) defines affordable housing cost as not exceeding 30% of gross income.

eligibility_rules.label: Initial down payment ≤ 5% of the unit's market value (market value unknown)

requirements_not_automated: Nonprofit organizational clearance for the welfare exemption
Recorded agreement terms (45 years, first-time low-income buyers, ≤5% down payment, affordable housing cost)
Officer affidavit to the County Assessor and construction-timing conditions
Qualifying lien dates and proration by the County Assessor
County Assessor determination

source.title: BOE Letter to Assessors No. 2023/044 — Welfare exemption: low-income housing (RTC §214.15.1)

programs.name: Nonprofit homeownership welfare exemption — zero-interest loan sales (RTC §214.15)
programs.how_it_works: Since 1999, may exempt nonprofit-owned property used to build or rehabilitate homes sold to low-income buyers when the sale is financed with a zero-interest loan. Cannot be stacked with §214.15.1 for the same tax expense.
programs.availability_note: Described in BOE LTA 2023/044 as in effect since October 10, 1999.

eligibility_rules.label: Buyer's purchase financed with a zero-interest loan
eligibility_rules.conflict_note: The model finances buyers at a {value:pct} mortgage rate; §214.15 requires a zero-interest-rate loan.

requirements_not_automated: Nonprofit organizational clearance for the welfare exemption
Zero-interest buyer financing structure
County Assessor determination

source.title: BOE Letter to Assessors No. 2023/044 (describes RTC §214.15 and §214.15.1)

programs.name: HCD CalHome Program
programs.how_it_works: State homeownership program for local agencies and nonprofits (development and buyer assistance). Assistance may be a grant, a forgivable development loan or a deferred buyer loan depending on activity — each has different effects on the gap.
programs.availability_note: The HCD CalHome page showed “Application window CLOSED — No longer accepting applications” when checked on 2026-11-07. Recheck before planning on it.

eligibility_rules.label: Applicant is a nonprofit or local agency

requirements_not_automated: An open NOFA / application round
Eligible activity and cost restrictions
Award amount and loan vs grant terms
Subsidy-layering compatibility with the city grant

programs.name: CalHFA MyHome Assistance
programs.how_it_works: Deferred-payment junior loan for down payment/closing costs through participating lenders. It helps the buyer, not the developer: it is not a developer grant and is never subtracted from the development gap.
programs.availability_note: Organizers' source list read the program page as up to 3.5% (FHA) / 3% (conventional). Terms and buyer eligibility not re-checked by the team.
requirements_not_automated: Buyer income and first-time status
Participating lender and first-mortgage compatibility
Compatibility with the project's resale restrictions

programs.name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program
programs.how_it_works: Federal funds administered by states and participating jurisdictions for affordable housing, including homeownership development or buyer assistance. Uses the separate State HOME income-limit table.
programs.availability_note: Availability through the City of Santa Ana or HCD not checked.
requirements_not_automated: Participating jurisdiction allocation and open round
HOME income limits (State HOME table) and affordability period
Federal cross-cutting requirements

source.title: HUD Exchange — HOME Investment Partnerships Program

programs.name: Self-Help Homeownership Opportunity Program (SHOP)
programs.how_it_works: HUD funds for sweat-equity / volunteer-based homeownership, notably land acquisition and infrastructure — restricted capital, not an unrestricted development grant. A simulation is capped at modeled land + site work.
programs.availability_note: Funds flow through national SHOP grantees; access for this project not checked.
requirements_not_automated: Affiliation with a national SHOP grantee
Sweat-equity requirements
Eligible uses (land/infrastructure) and per-unit limits

programs.name: SB 937 / local impact-fee deferral
programs.how_it_works: Delays when certain development fees are paid, reducing upfront cash needs. A deferral changes timing, not the fee amount — it does not reduce the permanent funding gap.
programs.availability_note: From the team's research table; no primary source linked yet. Check Santa Ana's current written fee rules before relying on it.
requirements_not_automated: The city's current written fee-deferral rule for this project
Which fees are deferrable and until when

source.title: Team research table (2026-11-07) — primary source not yet linked

programs.name: Local impact-fee waiver
programs.how_it_works: A city may waive or reduce eligible development fees for affordable homes — a real cost reduction only if a written waiver applies. HomeForge does not model fees as a separate line, so no savings are simulated.
programs.availability_note: From the team's research table; Santa Ana's waiver rules not checked.
requirements_not_automated: The city's written waiver rule and eligible fees
A fee line in the budget to reduce

source.title: Team research table (2026-11-07) — primary source not yet linked

programs.name: State Density Bonus Law
programs.how_it_works: More homes per parcel, reduced parking and development-standard concessions. A regulatory benefit, not funding.
programs.availability_note: This project already uses it: City Reso 2024-10 p.5 allows three additional units under the State Density Bonus Law.

source.title: Team research table (2026-11-07); project use documented in Santa Ana Reso 2024-10 p.5

programs.name: SB 684 / SB 1123 small-lot streamlining
programs.how_it_works: Streamlined approvals for qualifying developments of up to 10 homes — saves time (and carrying cost) on future sites; this site's map is already approved.
programs.availability_note: From the team's research table; statute text not read by the team.
requirements_not_automated: Statutory eligibility (zoning, lot size, unit count)
